title: Designing Cloud Servers for Lower Carbon
problem: Cloud compute servers are responsible for the majority of emissions in hyperscale cloud computing, and current server designs do not optimize for carbon efficiency. Designing practical, production-deployable carbon-efficient server SKUs requires addressing multiple constraints including performance requirements and data center overheads.
motivation: Reducing carbon emissions from hyperscale cloud computing is critical for climate change mitigation.
method: The authors design three GreenSKUs using low-carbon components including energy-efficient CPUs, reused old DRAM via CXL interconnect, and reused old SSDs. They develop GSF (GreenSKU Framework), a methodology to systematically evaluate carbon savings at scale within Azure's production constraints, accounting for data center overheads and performance requirements.
key_novelty: The GreenSKU Framework (GSF) provides a systematic methodology for evaluating carbon savings of server SKUs at scale within production cloud infrastructure while maintaining performance and data center compatibility.
contributions: Design of three carbon-efficient GreenSKUs using low-carbon components (energy-efficient CPUs, reused DRAM via CXL, reused SSDs)
Development of GSF methodology and framework for systematically evaluating carbon savings at scale
Implementation within Azure production constraints achieving 28% emissions reduction per core compared to deployed servers
Demonstration of 8% net cloud emission reduction considering data center overheads

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 28% emissions per core reduction vs currently-deployed servers
metrics.other: 15% emissions reduction when meeting performance requirements; 8% net cloud emissions reduction including data center overheads

limitations: Specific technical and adoption challenges are mentioned but not elaborated in depth within the abstract.
